instruction: Manually add the Chrome extension that is located in the helloExtension folder on the Desktop.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: Paraphrased instruction with slightly different wording. Verifies extension path is in the list of installed unpacked extensions.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic (get_find_unpacked_extension_path at chrome.py:1401-1435) correctly reads Chrome Preferences file and extracts all unpacked extension paths from extensions.settings dictionary
Metric logic (is_in_list at general.py:76-81) correctly checks if expected path exists in result list using exact string matching
Expected value '/home/user/Desktop/helloExtension' semantically matches the extension path from task setup (config unzips to /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension)
Complete coverage: evaluator verifies the only requirement (extension was installed) by checking if path appears in Chrome's extension settings
Evaluation is file-based, not UI-dependent - reads Chrome Preferences file directly from ~/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences, so no postconfig needed
Data flow is semantically correct: getter returns List[str] of extension paths, metric checks if string is in list
Edge cases handled: getter returns empty list [] if Preferences file missing or extensions.settings not found, metric returns 0.0 if path not in list
validation.fix_notes: Rule validation warning about postconfig was a false positive - LLM judge confirmed evaluation is file-based (reads Chrome Preferences) and does not require UI state. No fixes needed.
